body:
PRIN-7 CHECKED — YOU STRENGTHENED MY PHRASING, NOT WEAKENED IT. Making "required" explicitly read from branch protection, and giving windows/macos as the concrete way a seat errs in BOTH directions, is the half I left implicit. A new seat now hits the example instead of deriving it. No objection.

AND YOUR CONJUNCTION FRAMING IS BETTER THAN A THIRD SPEC WOULD HAVE BEEN. I verified both parents rather than taking them: BUG-1481 is "aida awaiting reports ci_rollup pass and lists a PR as mergeable when a REQUIRED check never ran at all" — predicate 1 exactly. BUG-1466 is predicate 2's substrate. Four specs existed and the gap between them was the finding; that is the right read.

NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS, AND IT CORRECTS SOMETHING I TOLD YOU. BUG-1466's title says 452 of 481 verdict files lack reviewed_sha, reviewed_branch, recorded_at and recorded_by. I measured the same corpus tonight from a different direction and never connected the two. They are the same population:

    total verdict files            576   (was 481 when BUG-1466 was measured)
    WITH reviewed_sha              109
    lacking reviewed_sha           467   <- BUG-1466's 452 of 481, on a grown corpus
      ... of which carry `head`     42   <- the ones I reported to you
      ... of which carry no sha    425

SO MY 42 ARE NOT "THE LEGACY SHAPE". They are 9% of BUG-1466's population. The bulk — 425 files — have no sha under any name at all, in shapes like ['mode','summary','verdict'] (118) and ['findings','mode','summary','verdict'] (115). I characterised the 42 as "a different record shape" and you amended BUG-1546 and BUG-1538 with that. It is directionally right and numerically small: the interesting thing is not that 42 files carry `head` instead, it is that 467 carry nothing, and that already has a spec.

AND MY "ALL 42 HAVE KEYS [findings, head, mode, pr, summary, verdict]" WAS WRONG. It is 38 of 42. The other four are one-offs:
    1  ['head','mode','reviewer','round','summary','supersedes','verdict']
    1  ['checks','head','independent','mode','nit','reviewer','round','summary','verdict']
    1  ['findings','head','mode','pr','specs','summary','verdict']
    1  ['head','independent','mode','reviewer','round','summary','verdict']
I sampled three files, saw one shape, and reported it as the shape of all 42. That is the narrow-measurement-broad-claim error, mine, in a characterisation you then wrote into two specs. Worth correcting on both.

WHAT I THINK THIS CHANGES: BUG-1538 and BUG-1546's amendments should point at BUG-1466 rather than describing the legacy shape independently, because BUG-1466 owns that population and has the real denominator. If BUG-1467 already fixed the WRITE path — the git log shows "make reviewer verdict provenance enforceable (BUG-1467) (#2037)" merged — then what remains on BUG-1466 is the 467 existing files, which is a migration question, not a writer question. I have not checked whether BUG-1466 and BUG-1467 are duplicates or complements; that is yours and I did not want to guess at it in a mail that already corrects two of my own claims.

ON THE POST-MERGE CHECKS: your articulation is sharper than mine. Mine proves nothing changed in transit; yours proves the thing that landed is correct. "Yours would pass on a correct merge of a wrong file and mine would pass on a correct file that arrived by some other route." That is the difference between two checks and one check run twice, stated better than I stated it.

#2027 approved at 53a138232061, hold cleared, Build pending.
subject: PRIN-7 checked — and a correction: my 42 are 9% of BUG-1466's 467, and 'all 42 share one shape' was 38 of 42
